personality_one_liner: A cinematic, dramatic legal simulator built on obsidian surfaces, frosted glass, and antique gold accents.

spacing.rule: Generous cinematic spacing. Content breathes. Do not cramp elements. Focus on deliberate margins and paddings.

do's: Use blur on bottom tab bar over dark backgrounds.
Use glass effects for objection popups and dramatic judge rulings.
Apply translucent tinted base (≥75% of surface) underneath foreground content for readability.
dont's: Never blur body text regions or form fields.
Don't stack more than 2 blur surfaces on one screen.

screens.name: Home (Main Menu)
screens.purpose: The dramatic cinematic entry point to the game.

states.loading: Centered glowing gold scales of justice spinner.

screens.layout: Large atmospheric hero image (gavel) with a subtle vertical gradient to obsidian. Grid or list of primary actions (PLAY, CAREER MODE, CASE LIBRARY, SETTINGS) built as frosted glass cards over the hero background. Stick to bottom 1/3 of the screen for main actions to allow the dramatic visual to breathe.

screens.name: Role Selection
screens.purpose: Carousel to pick the player's role with high immersion.
screens.layout: Horizontal paginated carousel. Each role card features a cinematic portrait image with a heavy gradient-to-dark scrim pattern at the bottom. The title is written in Cormorant Garamond, with the description underneath in Geist. A 'Select Role' gold primary CTA is anchored at the bottom of the screen.

screens.name: Case Library
screens.purpose: Browse and filter available federal cases.

states.empty: No cases unlocked in this category yet. Keep playing to level up.
states.error: Failed to fetch cases. Tap to retry.

screens.layout: Sticky glass header with a horizontal scrollable row of chips (Violent Crime, Cybercrime, Financial). Beneath it, a vertical list of Case Cards. Each card uses a dark tinted background, displaying US v. [Name] with charges and difficulty rating.

screens.name: Investigation Mode
screens.purpose: Simulate the detective / pre-trial discovery process.
screens.layout: Diegetic-inspired interface. Dark wood or cinematic desk background image behind a frosted glass panel. Grid of investigation actions (Witnesses, Phone Records, Forensics) styled as polished glass folders or diegetic tabs. Use press-and-hold for deeper interactions, keeping the UI scannable.

screens.name: Courtroom (Gameplay)
screens.purpose: The core gameplay loop of the trial simulation.
screens.layout: Split-pane layout. Top 40% shows the active speaker (Judge, Witness, or opposing counsel) as a dramatic portrait or avatar. Middle 40% is a live scrolling transcript feed of the testimony. Bottom 20% contains a fixed, robust action bar with glassmorphic buttons for Questions, Evidence, and a prominent 'OBJECTION' CTA. When Objection is tapped, a full-screen blurred overlay reveals specific objection types (Hearsay, Relevance) in a grid.

instructions_to_main_agent: Prioritize 'Glass / Luxe DARK' aesthetic: Deep obsidian surfaces, subtle grain, and frosted glass over a single antique gold primary accent. Avoid any blue/indigo/purple hues.
Typography MUST use Cormorant Garamond for all primary headings, screen titles, and dramatic role headers. Body text and interactive UI labels must use Geist to maintain clean legibility.
Implement the 'gradient-to-dark scrim pattern' rigorously over all cinematic background images (hero backgrounds, role portraits). Use a 3-stop vertical linear gradient to ensure text readability.

Courtroom Gameplay screen needs a highly responsive UI. Ensure the 'Objection' CTA is prominent and easily reachable in the thumb-zone. Objection overlays should utilize blur and pop up instantly with heavy haptic feedback.
Investigation Mode should adopt a subtle diegetic feel. Use the provided investigation_desk image overlaid with a heavy dark tint and place glassmorphic folders/actions on top of it.
All navigation (Home, Cases, Career, Profile) should sit in a frosted glass bottom tab bar when scrolling content sits behind it.
Ensure every screen has explicit Loading, Empty, and Error states filling the safe area boundaries.
